title: 法律证据与合同条款审查

sources.title: UCC § 2-316 — Exclusion or Modification of Warranties (LII / Cornell Law School)
sources.key_facts: Subsection (2): to exclude merchantability warranty must 'mention merchantability and in case of a writing must be conspicuous'; fitness warranty exclusion requires 'a writing and conspicuous'. Subsection (3)(a): 'as is' or 'with all faults' language effectively excludes implied warranties if it reasonably alerts buyer.

sources.title: UCC § 2-719 — Contractual Modification or Limitation of Remedy (LII / Cornell Law School)
sources.key_facts: §2-719(1): agreement may limit or alter measure of damages recoverable; §2-719(2): 'Where circumstances cause an exclusive or limited remedy to fail of its essential purpose, remedy may be had as provided in this Act'; §2-719(3): consequential damages may be limited or excluded unless unconscionable; limitation for personal injury from consumer goods is 'prima facie unconscionable'.

sources.title: CISG Article 74 — Damages (CISG-online.org)
sources.key_facts: Exact text: 'Damages for breach of contract by one party consist of a sum equal to the loss, including loss of profit, suffered by the other party as a consequence of the breach. Such damages may not exceed the loss which the party in breach foresaw or ought to have foreseen at the time of the conclusion of the contract, in the light of the facts and matters of which he then knew or ought to have known, as a possible consequence of the breach of contract.' Single provision, no subsections.

sources.title: ICC Force Majeure and Hardship Clauses 2020 (International Chamber of Commerce)
sources.key_facts: ICC 2020 Force Majeure Clause: termination threshold is 120 days duration of impediment; either party may terminate without damages if impediment exceeds 120 days. Short-form and long-form versions available. Notification obligation separated into distinct clause; suspension of performance from day of notice.

sources.title: GDPR Article 28 — Processor (gdpr-info.eu)
sources.key_facts: Art.28(3): DPA 'shall be in writing, including in electronic form'. Required DPA elements: subject-matter, duration, nature, purpose, types of personal data, categories of data subjects, obligations/rights of controller. Sub-processors require prior written authorization. Processors must allow audits. Post-contract: processor deletes or returns all personal data. Penalties for non-compliance: up to €10,000,000 or 2% of global annual turnover, whichever is higher (via Art.83(4)).

sources.title: Everbridge Master Services Agreement v11 (January 2025)
sources.key_facts: Section 10 (Limitation of Liability): cap = fees paid in the 12-month period prior to when the claim arose; excludes indirect/incidental/consequential/lost profits damages. Section 9.1 (IP Indemnification): Company defends against IP infringement claims; remedies include procure rights / modify / replace functional equivalent / refund prepaid unused fees pro-rata. Section 5.3 (Termination for breach): 30-day written notice + 30-day cure period. Section 8.2 (Disclaimer): 'COMPANY PROVIDES THE SOLUTIONS AS IS'. Governing law: Delaware (US), Netherlands (EMEA non-UK), England (UK/ME), Singapore (APAC).

sources.title: AWS Customer Agreement (Amazon Web Services)
sources.key_facts: Section 9.2: aggregate liability capped at amounts paid for specific Services during preceding 12 months. Section 9.1: excludes indirect/incidental/consequential/exemplary damages, lost profits/revenues/goodwill. Section 7.2 (IP Indemnification): AWS indemnifies against IP infringement; remedies = procure rights / replace / modify / terminate + refund. Section 5.2(a): AWS termination for convenience = 30 days advance notice; Section 5.3(b): 30-day grace period post-termination to retrieve customer data (fees must be paid). AWS Confidential Info protection: 5 years post-Term.

sources.title: Hadley v Baxendale — Wikipedia
sources.key_facts: Case citation: Hadley & Anor v Baxendale & Ors [1854] EWHC J70; also cited as 9 Exch 341. Court: Exchequer Court. Date: 23 February 1854. Two-part Hadley Rule established by Baron Alderson: Rule 1 = general damages arising naturally from breach; Rule 2 = special consequential damages if breaching party had knowledge of special circumstances at contract formation. Key quoted language: 'damages which the other party ought to receive...should be such as may fairly and reasonably be considered either arising naturally...from such breach of contract itself, or such as may reasonably be supposed to have been in the contemplation of both parties.' Became Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 351.

sources.title: SaaS Agreements: Key Contractual Provisions (ABA Business Law Today, 2021)
sources.key_facts: Market standard for SaaS: overarching cap tied to multiple of monthly fees, e.g. 3 months minimum (customers typically negotiate 12 months). Common carve-outs from cap: IP infringement, gross negligence, willful misconduct, indemnification obligations. Cloud provider owns data but customer owns Customer Data and all IP rights. Required transition support upon termination. Courts may void liability limitations for recklessness/gross negligence causing substantial data loss.

sources.title: ICC Force Majeure Clause 2020 Analysis (Crowell & Moring LLP)
sources.key_facts: ICC 2020 update specifies 120-day threshold for contract termination due to force majeure impediment, replacing vague 'reasonable period' language from 2003 version. Two versions: short-form and comprehensive long-form. Affected party can suspend performance from day of notice.
